plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A graceful deciduous tree that covers its branches in clouds of pale pink to nearly white five-petaled blossoms before the leaves emerge. It is the most famous cherry blossom tree and the centerpiece of hanami celebrations.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), Korea, and temperate parks and gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The 3,000 cherry trees gifted by Tokyo to Washington D.C. in 1912 were mostly Yoshino cherries, and the National Cherry Blossom Festival celebrates their peak bloom around late March.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler yellow petals and narrow blue-green leaves. It grows in woodlands and meadows and is widely cultivated in gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late February to April in Northern Hemisphere temperate zones
plants.location: Western Europe, especially England, Wales, France, and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain lycorine and galantamine; the latter is derived from related plants and used in medicine for treating symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Magnolia stellata
plants.description: A small deciduous shrub or tree with fragrant, star-shaped flowers that have many strap-like petals. The blooms appear on bare branches in early spring and can be damaged by late frosts.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (March to April)
plants.location: Native to Japan; cultivated in temperate gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plants, evolving before bees existed, so their flowers are sturdy enough to withstand pollination by beetles.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: A bulbous plant that sends up leafless stalks topped with clusters of fragrant, funnel-shaped pink flowers. The strap-like leaves appear later, after the flowers fade. It blooms in the Southern Hemisphere's autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn in the Southern Hemisphere (February to April)
plants.location: Native to the Western Cape of South Africa; naturalized in Australia, New Zealand, and California
plants.funFact: Its nickname 'Naked Lady' comes from the way the flower stems burst from the ground without any leaves, often appearing overnight after autumn rains.
